answer: The juniper report makes public the merge explicitly at each kernel. Each collapsed cluster gets one copper weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 123 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 225 times the capital for one share. A farm of 3893 identities would post 1300 proofs and burn roughly 87 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
